records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new `s.search.TotalDocs()` call in the init success log assumes every search backend implements TotalDocs and returns meaningful data at this point, but no test in the diff asserts the log line or that TotalDocs is safe to call immediately after build completes. If TotalDocs panics or returns zero for file-backed indexes (the bleve file path was just touched in this same PR), the 'search index initialized' success path itself fails after startup completes, converting a log statement into a crash — with the postgres integration test skipped, no automated run would catch it.
records.rationale: The diff adds a new init success log line that calls into the search backend: `s.log.Info("search index initialized", "duration_secs", end-start, "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())` (pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go). This introduces a new runtime dependency during startup on `TotalDocs()` being implemented and safe to call immediately after `s.search.init(ctx)` finishes. The diff does not show any tests covering this new code path, and the PR also adds a postgres skip to an integration test (`t.Skip("... test not working with postgres ...")`), reducing automated coverage. records.issue_text: [BUG] Moving s.Init(ctx) into NewResourceServer converts a per-request failure into a hard constructor failure, changing the deployment contract of the resource server. Any embedding of the unified storage server where the search index or backend init fails (e.g. corrupt bleve index dir, DB temporarily unavailable at boot) now crashes/exits the whole Grafana process at startup instead of returning errors per request as before — this behavioral contract change was made in a PR titled 'performance optimizations' with no stated intent to change failure semantics.
records.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization/error propagation semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure (server.go @@255+), while the prior per-request `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` checks were removed from many handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob). This converts what used to be request-time errors into constructor-time failure, which can impact embeddings/startup behavior even if not a strictly verifiable correctness bug from the diff alone.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Moving s.Init(ctx) into NewResourceServer converts a previously per-request, retryable initialization into a hard constructor failure that aborts startup. Operators running multi-node Grafana: any transient failure during index building or watcher initialization (e.g., slow DB, bleve directory lock, network blip) that previously failed one request and retried on the next now prevents the resource server (and the process embedding it) from starting at all, turning a partial degradation into a full outage across the fleet on restart.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the cacheMu lock from the body of BuildIndex and only locking around the final cache assignment allows two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource to both call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory. During rolling restarts or concurrent index rebuilds of large tenants (size > FileThreshold), two goroutines open the same file-backed bleve index at the same path simultaneously; one of the resulting indexes is discarded from the cache while its on-disk directory remains, and concurrent writes to the same bleve directory can leave a corrupted/partial index that later builds must rebuild from scratch — an availability and disk-state issue, not just a perf nit.
records.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously took b.cacheMu for the whole function and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx` (removed `b.cacheMu.Lock()/defer Unlock()` at the top; added lock/unlock only at the end).
